title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v11)
author: Marta Kovács
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token cost and tail latency caused by naive padding when batching heterogeneous sequence lengths. This PR implements a new dynamic-bucketing heuristic that groups requests by sequence-length clusters then applies a padding-minimization schedule and KV-cache alignment to avoid unnecessary KV materialization. The heuristic is cost-driven: it evaluates expected token-padding overhead against queuing latency to pick when to wait for additional similar-length requests. It includes kernel-friendly padding targets so the runtime selects optimized attention kernels and reduces kernel launch overhead. Changes include: 1) seqlen bucket manager with online clustering, 2) greedy cost function with adjustable latency vs cost weights, 3) padding target policy that biases to hardware-friendly sequence lengths, 4) KV cache alignment to buckets to avoid per-request cache reshaping and copies, 5) scheduler integration for continuous batching with per-bucket max-wait and burst windows, and 6) telemetry and perf tests. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and config flags. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for bucket manager - [x] end-to-end perf harness updates - [x] KV cache zero-copy integration tests - [x] docs/console flags for operators - [x] canary rollout plan in ENG-9370

perf_summary: Canary on dedicated pool (g5-8) with mixed seqlen workload: average tokens/sec +14% on bursty arrival patterns, token-cost reduction ~12% due to less padding, P95 latency improved ~8% under steady load. Tail queuing in extreme skewed workloads unchanged vs baseline due to conservative default latency_weight. Memory overhead peak +3% when many buckets active; aligner cap prevents OOMs.
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching by grouping requests into sequence-length buckets, minimizing padding and aligning KV cache to buckets. Results: lower token costs and improved P95 latency for mixed-length workloads. Config flags: seqlen_bucket.enabled, seqlen_bucket.latency_weight, seqlen_bucket.max_wait_ms, seqlen_bucket.padding_targets. Can be toggled via console feature flag for canary rollout.
notes_for_ops: Default config is conservative to preserve latency SLOs. Recommend ramping seqlen_bucket.latency_weight from 0.7 to 0.5 in non-latency-sensitive environments to favor cost savings. Monitor metrics: dynbatch.bucket_padding_overhead, dynbatch.bucket_queue_time_ms, kv.align_copy_bytes.
